account:
Today there seems to be a larger private gathering being prepared in the great hall behind the description of a lighting inspection. Baker, innkeeper, freight, and secretary were involved in early-morning arrangements. I am due at the hall at eighteen with the builder; the innkeeper repeatedly asked me to attend, although the appointment was already confirmed. The baker calls the bread 'jubilee bread' and says two hundred loaves were prepared. Freight said he delivered 160 to the table chest at minus fifty, thirty, and the baker later said he delivered thirty-two and that the bakery bread chest was empty. I have not personally checked the hall's contents or accounted for the remaining eight loaves.

The innkeeper says he commissioned the bread for an inn hospitality arrangement and will settle the account privately. The secretary's report instead records freight calling it his order and giving the baker twenty-four emeralds and seventy-two wheat, with another 528 wheat then needed. Those statements may describe different parts of the same arrangement, rather than wrongdoing. I also overheard the baker asking the innkeeper for settlement and a promised thirty-emerald repayment. No town payment has been authorized.

My suspicion is that the lighting inspection is a pretext for a jubilee celebration or surprise gathering, possibly involving me, but nobody has told me whose jubilee it is. I cannot yet establish its real purpose. Separately, people near the mill have repeated the odd phrase 'bridge or port change at bakery'; I do not know what it means or whether it connects to the preparations. I have kept my morning office appointment and am now at the mill for the scheduled grain inspection, with the secretary and report. Grain availability and delivery terms still need confirmation.
